title: Relation Between Refractive Indices
notes:
## 1. Topic Introduction — Chaining Media Together

Light travels from water into glass — how do their refractive indices combine? The relation between refractive indices lets you jump between any pair of media using air (or vacuum) as the common currency, and it explains why pools look shallow and spearfishing takes aim below the target.

## 2. Fundamental Concepts (NEB 2024)

### 2.1 Relative and absolute indices

- **Relative refractive index of medium 2 with respect to medium 1:**
$$n_{21} = \frac{n_2}{n_1} = \frac{v_1}{v_2} = \frac{\sin i}{\sin r}$$
- The index of medium 1 w.r.t. 2 is simply the reciprocal: $n_{12} = \dfrac{1}{n_{21}}$.
- **Absolute** indices (w.r.t. vacuum) chain: if light goes 1 → 2 → 3, the effective relative index $n_{31} = \dfrac{n_3}{n_1}$, and intermediate media don't change the final bending.

### 2.2 Real and apparent depth

When looking vertically into a denser medium of index n:
$$\text{apparent depth} = \frac{\text{real depth}}{n}$$
Objects under water appear raised — the pool looks shallower, the fish looks higher. Conversely, viewed from below, objects above appear farther.

### 2.3 Worked numericals

**Q (3m, 2024):** A fish is 1.2 m below the water surface (μ = 4/3). At what apparent depth does it appear to an observer above the surface?
$$\text{apparent depth} = \frac{\text{real depth}}{\mu} = \frac{1.2}{4/3} = 1.2 \times \frac{3}{4} = 0.9 \text{ m}$$
The fish appears raised — spear-fishing must aim **below** the seen position.

**Q (NEB-style):** Light passes from water (n = 4/3) into glass (n = 3/2). Find n_glass,water.
$n_{g,w} = \dfrac{n_g}{n_w} = \dfrac{1.5}{4/3} = \dfrac{4.5}{4} = 1.125$.

**Q (NEB-style):** A tank appears 1.8 m deep. If n_water = 4/3, find its real depth.
Real depth = apparent × n = $1.8 \times \frac{4}{3} = 2.4$ m.

## 3. Conceptual Relationships

- **To Topic 70:** the relative index IS the Snell's-law constant.
- **To Topic 73:** the same geometry, at grazing incidence, defines the critical angle.
- **To apparent bending of a stick:** refraction at the surface shifts the apparent position of every submerged point.

## 4. Exam Orientation and Previous Year Questions (NEB)

### 4.1 Verified PYQs from the solved-paper bank

| Year | Unit | Topic | Question | Marks | Type |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2080/2024 | Optics | Refraction | A fish is 1.2 m below the water surface (μ = 4/3). At what apparent depth does it appear to an observer above the surface? | 3 | Numerical |

### 4.2 Likely additional forms (NEB-style)

1. Define relative refractive index and write n₂₁ in terms of n₁ and n₂ (2m).
2. Real depth from apparent depth (2–3m).
3. Show n₂₁ = v₁/v₂ (3m).

### 4.3 Common examination mistakes

1. Inverting the fraction: apparent depth = real/n, not real × n.
2. Mixing absolute and relative indices in one equation.
3. Forgetting that n₁₂ = 1/n₂₁.

```svg Reversibility: n₂₁ = 1/n₁₂
<svg viewBox="0 0 640 240" font-family="Segoe UI" font-size="13"><rect x="0" y="0" width="640" height="240" fill="#ffffff"/><g text-anchor="middle"><rect x="110" y="60" width="180" height="110" rx="8" fill="#eff6ff" stroke="#1d4ed8"/><text x="200" y="120" fill="#1d4ed8">water n = 1.33</text><rect x="370" y="60" width="180" height="110" rx="8" fill="#fefce8" stroke="#a16207"/><text x="460" y="120" fill="#a16207">glass n = 1.5</text><text x="320" y="210" fill="#374151">n_wg = n_g/n_w ≈ 1.13</text></g></svg>
```

**Relative index — relations classified**

| Quantity | Formula | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Relative | n21 = n2/n1 | Medium 2 wrt 1 |
| Reciprocal | n12 = 1/n21 | Reversing order |
| Product | n12 x n21 = 1 | Round trip |
